subject: Post-call: E2E latency probing — targets, streaming, and demo scheduling
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
To: Amelia Chen <amelia@apexhealth.ai>, Tom Rivera <tom@apexhealth.ai>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.inference, logan.wright@redwood.inference
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: E2E latency probing — targets, streaming, and demo scheduling

Hi Amelia / Tom — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can reproduce and validate end-to-end: 

Summary of targets you mentioned on the call:
- p95 end-to-end generation (client -> Redwood hosted API -> responses returned): <= 200 ms
- p99 end-to-end: <= 450 ms
- Typical prompt size: ~40 tokens output average (50 token worst-case bursts)
- Streaming requirement: chunking interval at client should be <= 120 ms; we need to validate chunked delivery latency under load
- Concurrency/throughput: steady concurrent connections ~50 QPS, expected bursts up to 200 concurrent requests for ~5-10 minutes during peak jobs

What we need from your side to scope the verification run:
1) Sample traffic profile (CSV or trace) showing per-request size distribution and timestamps (a 1-hour sample is fine).
2) Incumbent provider logs/summary of their p95/p99 for a comparable trace (sample file is great).
3) A service account or short-lived API key we can use in a controlled test sandbox (we'll only run read-only workload).
4) Confirmation that streaming will be exercised with existing client (or whether we should run a synthetic streaming client).

Proposed plan / timeline:
- Demo & hands-on verification slot: Tue 12 May, 10:00 AM PT (30–45 min) — we’ll show a live run and capture p95/p99 under two profiles (steady, burst).
- Technical verification window: Wed 13 May, 2-hour window where Redwood will run controlled load against your staging endpoint to produce p95/p99 numbers and side-by-side comparison with incumbent traces.

Attachments: I’ll include a short test-plan doc and calendar invite after internal alignment.

Next steps from me (today): confirm internal test plan with Aditya and Logan, share demo invite, and send a short checklist for the data you’ll provide.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference
(415) 555-0192

--
Note: We will treat any sample traces as confidential — happy to sign an NDA if needed.

From: Amelia Chen <amelia@apexhealth.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom@apexhealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 16:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: E2E latency probing — targets, streaming, and demo scheduling

Thanks Vanessa — left a few notes inline.

Quick clarifications:
- The 200ms p95 is our target for perceived latency; pragmatic acceptance threshold is p95 <= 250 ms. p99 target is ideally <= 450 ms but acceptable up to 500 ms during bursts.
- Our current provider (IncumbentAI) reports for our production trace: p95 = 320 ms, p99 = 820 ms (attached sample). That’s why reducing tail latency is a priority.
- Streaming: our client emits token chunks every 80–120ms; we need to ensure that Redwood's streaming path consistently beats the incumbent (both in median and tail).

Attached "incumbent_metrics.csv" — includes timestamps and response durations for a 30-minute peak window. Feel free to use a synthetic client if easier; we can also enable a staging API key for you (I’ll loop in our infra owner if you need a service account).

We can make Tue 12 May 10:00 AM PT for the demo. Please send the calendar invite + meeting link.

Best,
Amelia Chen
Head of ML Platform | Apex Health
amelia@apexhealth.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>

Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 16:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: E2E latency probing — targets, streaming, and demo scheduling

Vanessa — quick internal plan:

- Test plan (high level):
  * Baseline single-connection streaming run (no KV cache) to measure pure serve latency for 40-token outputs.
  * Steady-state run: 50 concurrent connections for 30 minutes; capture p50/p95/p99, network RTT, and chunk intervals.
  * Burst run: ramp to 200 concurrent for 10 minutes (simulate their peak). Collect per-token and end-to-end traces.
- Model & infra: recommend using redwood-alpha-2 (2.7B quantized profile) on hosted cluster for initial runs — gives representative latency while preserving cost. If they request exact parity to their production model, we can swap.
- Observability: enable request-id propagation and include their trace IDs when available to map to incumbent traces.
- Data/credentials: we only need a staging API key and the sample trace (attached by Amelia). No PII expected in traces.

Logan — can you draft the short runbook and a 2-page test-plan PDF (I’ll review) so Vanessa can attach it to the invite?

Aditya
Sr. Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Amelia / Tom — thanks for the prompt reply and for attaching the incumbent trace. I pulled the key asks below and attached a concise test plan and calendar invite for Tue 12 May 10:00 AM PT.

What Redwood will run during the demo (brief):
- Live streaming demo showing chunk delivery and per-chunk latencies.
- Two verification runs using your sample profile: steady 50 concurrent and 10-min burst to 200 concurrent.
- We’ll produce p50/p95/p99 snapshots and a short side-by-side comparison with the supplied incumbent trace.

Items we still need from you before Wed 13 May verification window: 
1) Short-lived staging API key (or a service account with permissions for test runs).
2) Confirmation whether to keep client-side chunking at 80–120ms or let Redwood control chunk emission during tests.
3) Any protective headers/allowlists we need to know about for your staging network.

Deliverables after the verification run: final p95/p99 report, CSV of raw latencies, and a 2-page summary that maps improvements to unit cost delta (if applicable).

Calendar: demo invite attached ("demo-invite.ics"). Test plan attached as PDF.

If that all looks good I’ll lock the Tue demo and ping infra at Apex for the staging key.

Thanks — talk soon,
Vanessa Ortiz
